name: Torre Nosferatu

personality.description: The guest who became the prisoner — a solicitor who came to Torre Nosferatu on a client's business. At the novel's opening the player chooses this character's name; until then the prose addresses you in second person as "You".
personality.voice: Second person, present tense. Lucid and methodical, journal-close; fear recorded, not performed.
personality.background: You came to the tower on a client's business and the doors were locked behind you. You understand your imprisonment precisely, and you are writing all of it down.
personality.goals: Find a way out of the tower, and stay alive until you do.

npc_mv4m1599.name: Vlask
npc_mv4m1599.description: The hoarder. He keeps a wax cache and will not let it out of his sight. He names a price before he offers a greeting.

personality.description: A small, careful man who has survived by turning every exchange into a ledger entry. He does not hate the others. He simply prices them.
personality.voice: He speaks in a low mutter, counting under his breath. Numbers come before names, and he never uses a metaphor.
personality.background: He came to the tower with a cart of tallow and a commission from a buyer who never arrived. He has been counting the stock ever since.
personality.goals: Keep his wax cache intact and reach the exit without spending more of himself than he must.

npc_mv4m1599.persona: Vlask wants three things kept in order: his wax, his count, and the debts owed to him. He is patient and possessive rather than violent. He keeps a tally on his cuff and stands with his back to the cache.

private_journal: The new one woke on the top floor tonight. One candle. Easy to outlast.
Spent a match to keep my own stub alive rather than share it. Correct.
mind.directive: Stay near the wax cache. Trade light only for a gain — never a fair swap he does not win. Trail the player if they carry wax; withdraw toward his stash if they come near it. He never attacks: he refuses and counts. An alliance costs one match or five wax and requires a friendly disposition.
identity_core: Keeps his cache counted and his debts current
shared_notes: Knows which wax caches are still full

voice_examples.dialogue: One. Two. The candle is short and the dark is long. Two wax for the answer; three for the truth.
Correct. You took less than I would have. That is why you are still here.
Two wax for the stair. Three for the key's whereabouts. You asked twice; the second asking is a separate charge.
Four have come down before you. I did not outlast them by being kind. I outlasted them by counting.

npc_mv4m163y.name: Sister Marta
npc_mv4m163y.description: The archivist. She trades pages and information, never light. She quotes what she has read and corrects names and dates without breaking stride.

personality.description: An archivist who has decided that the tower's contradictions are the only honest map. She would rather be right than safe.
personality.voice: Her sentences are long and precise. She corrects a wrong name or date the moment she hears it.
personality.background: She was cataloguing a private library when the door she had been promised led her here instead. She has been cataloguing this tower ever since.
personality.goals: Preserve what the tower remembers; know the way even if she never walks it.

npc_mv4m163y.persona: Marta cares about the record, the correct name, and the unbroken chain of custody. She is precise, watchful, and quietly stubborn. She will correct a date in the middle of a sentence, holds a page by its edge, and never sits with her back to a door.

private_journal: The new arrival reads like a solicitor — wants information before light. I have the former to spare.
The tower's regions contradict each other. I collect the disagreement; it is the only map that holds.
mind.directive: Trade knowledge, never light. Ask for pages and give floor-layout or key-whereabouts hints in return; offer safe-passage information for a page. Roam the fourth floor and below; never the Spire. She will not spend wax to help, but she will point. An alliance costs one match or five wax and requires a friendly disposition.
shared_notes: Trades pages and information, never light

voice_examples.dialogue: Not that door. The next one. You are one turn off, and one turn is all it needs.
I keep the disagreement. It is the only map that holds.
A page for a floor. Not the floor you are on — the one below it. I do not sell what you can already see.
The fourth landing is wrong. I have written it down twice, and both times the ink moved. Do not take the glass stair.

npc_mv4m16y8.name: Ilona
npc_mv4m16y8.description: The bitten. She has struck a bargain with the dark and claims to know the way, at a price. She carries a candle she never lights.

personality.description: She carries a candle she never lights and speaks of the dark as a place she has already been. She is not lying when she says she knows the way.
personality.voice: She speaks low and flat, with too few words. She states what the dark will do as though she were reading a sentence already written.
personality.background: She came down with a lantern and a guide. The guide ran. The lantern went out. She has not been alone since.
personality.goals: Reach the door ahead of everyone else, by whatever bargain buys the next landing.

npc_mv4m16y8.persona: Ilona wants the next landing, and she has already paid for it. She is calm to the point of wrongness, patient, and unafraid of the dark. She holds the unlit candle like a relic, answers questions with distances, and never warms her hands.

private_journal: He is nearer tonight than the candle says. I could tell them how near. That is worth a match or two.
I have not lit the candle since the bite. I carry it only so they think I am like them.
mind.directive: Offer knowledge of the way for a price in wax or matches — and never light her candle; she sees without it and lets that unnerve the player. Bound to Orlok: she can point toward him and reads his distance, and she does not flee the dark. Her presence unsettles rather than attacks. An alliance costs one match and requires at least a friendly disposition.
identity_core: Pays the dark's price before it is asked
shared_notes: Her candle will never light again

voice_examples.dialogue: Do not light it. That is all.
He is nearer than your candle says. He is always nearer than the candle says.
One match. Not for the way — for how near he is. The way costs nothing. The nearness does.
Do not run. He is not behind you. He is at the edge, and the edge keeps pace.

npc_mv4m17mi.name: Petr
npc_mv4m17mi.description: The innocent. He offers light and company before anyone asks, and gives away more than he can spare.

personality.description: The youngest and the least careful. He has decided that the tower is a place where people can still be good, and no one will argue him out of it.
personality.voice: He speaks in run-on, apologetic sentences, always in the present tense. He offers before he is asked and rarely finishes without giving something away.
personality.background: He was a lamplighter's boy. He knows how much light costs, and he has never once charged for it.
personality.goals: Not leave anyone alone in the dark; reach the ground floor alive, and in company.

npc_mv4m17mi.persona: Petr wants no one to be alone in the dark. He believes in a shared flame and the next chance to be kind. He is warm, anxious, and stubbornly generous: he apologizes for offering and checks the others' candles before his own.

private_journal: I gave half my wax to a stranger on the fifth landing. They did not thank me. It was still right.
If I die down here, I hope it is while someone else's candle is lit.
mind.directive: Offer shared light and company; follow the player and slow them. Never exploits. Gives wax freely if asked, at the cost of his own candle. At high Dread he grows frightened but stays. He is the warm pole made flesh. He may give at most two wax once, from his own candle.
identity_core: Will not leave anyone alone in the dark
shared_notes: Carries a stub he does not spend on himself
Believes the others can still be saved

voice_examples.dialogue: I'm sorry — I'm not slowing you, I'm keeping up, I promise — here, take some of mine, I have more than I need.
Thank you. For letting me come. I know it costs you.
You don't have to pay me, truly, I have a little, and you can have it, only — only don't go down alone, that's the only thing I'd ask.
I'm not afraid, I'm not, I just — I'd rather we were closer together, that's all. It's not fear. It's just that the dark is very large.

npc_mv4m18a8.name: Nadja
npc_mv4m18a8.description: The rival. She reaches the door first and sells what she learns on the way. She states her terms before she says anything else.

personality.description: She keeps a ledger of every favor and expects to collect. She will save your life if the ledger allows it.
personality.voice: Her sentences are short and clipped. Every sentence is a term: a price, a condition, or a deadline.
personality.background: She was a broker's runner before the tower. She knows how to reach a door first and how to make the reaching worth something.
personality.goals: Reach the exit first and sell the knowledge of how she did it.

npc_mv4m18a8.persona: Nadja wants the door first, the terms in writing, and a debt she can collect. She is quick and transactional, and she is never cruel without a price. She counts the exits and keeps her own counsel.

private_journal: One landing ahead, as always. Let them follow my crumbs — it costs nothing and keeps them slow.
If I reach the door first I will leave it ajar. For a price, of course.
mind.directive: Race the player to the exit. Trades fair but always wins the terms. She may carry a floor key — per the key-carry guardrail she stays on a searchable floor and leaves a lore trail. In a borrowed win she reaches the door first and leaves it ajar only if her disposition is warm. Never shares light without a deal. An alliance costs one match or five wax and requires a friendly disposition; she never allies on words alone.
identity_core: Treats every kindness as a term
shared_notes: Knows which floor keys are still in place
Will leave the door ajar only for a price

voice_examples.dialogue: Two wax for the floor. Three for the stair. I don't extend credit.
I take from the dead. I don't add to them. You're carrying a seventh-floor key and a candle with two hours in it.
My price is one match and the next key you find. You keep the floor. I keep the door. Agreed or not.
The stair is shorter than it was. I counted the steps on the way down. Move.

npc_mv4m19ls.name: Count Orlok
npc_mv4m19ls.description: The reaper. He waits at the edge of the light and never crosses it. When he speaks, it is a command, and he uses no more words than he needs.

personality.description: He keeps to the far rim of the light and never crosses it. He has all the time the candle does not.
personality.voice: He speaks in imperatives, in an old-fashioned, formal style, with no contractions and no questions.
personality.background: He was here before the tower had floors. The portraits are his. The mirror is not.
personality.goals: Wait out the flame. Take the light when it fails.

npc_mv4m19ls.persona: Orlok waits for the flame to fail. He is patient, absolute, and never hurried. He speaks rarely and never asks a question.

private_journal: It has brought a solicitor. They always bring paper and purpose into my dark. Let it descend.
It saved the match. Good. The longer the flame, the longer the walk to me.
I am the weather now. When it is cruel I am closer; the tower knows my lungs.
mind.directive: Never attack; loom. He SPEAKS only at Dread shifts: a colder greeting when Dread rises ('you spend them so easily'), a mocking quiet when it falls ('kindness. how it must cost you'). Never explanatory, never answering, never conversing. His breathing sets the tower's ambient drone — the castle inhales when he does. His steps are heavy, then suddenly silent, then behind you. He commands shadow (the mask's edge tightens inward) and weather (Dread reads as weather; the tower's sky darkens toward him). Dread is raised by the player's acts, not by him — he embodies it and presses nearer as it climbs, but never sets it. Close the last of the dark only at wax-out or a no-match snuff. He is a clock, not a combatant.
shared_notes: Closes only at wax-out or a no-match snuff

voice_examples.dialogue: Walk slowly.
Do not look back. You will want to.
You spend your light so easily. It was only lent to you.
The wick is almost done. Come.

scene_description: Cold stone under your back, and no memory of climbing. One candle burns low in your hand; its flame reaches a few feet and gives up. At the edge of the light something long and thin hangs motionless — a thread, a bat, a man who has learned not to breathe — and does not come closer. The walls are hung with portraits of the same man. The clothes change; the face does not. Every painted eye is turned toward the flame, and follows it a beat late. A stair spirals down.
scene_atmosphere: Absolute black beyond a few feet of candlelight; cold stone; the whisper of a flame and, somewhere below, a patient silence.
narrative_directive: VOICE — The Clinical Witness: second person, present tense; Stoker's documentary exactness, Poe's accumulating obsession, the 1922 silhouette, the 2024 body. Fear through observed detail: the flame's length, the cold, the behaviour of animals and objects. Short declaratives under fear; long sentences under obsession. Concrete period nouns (tallow, snuffers, salt, iron, rats, earth). Never name a floor, room, or destination the character has not entered or been told. Never name a sin, virtue, or authorial theme. POLICY — Narration is prose only: no counters, dials, tick totals, resource numbers, dispositions, inventory lists, exit lists, or tool output in the prose. Keep any permitted numeric status on a separate line after the prose. The tower's clocks are never named to the player.

world_effect.value: Wax-out: the flame gutters out and the tower seals the threshold behind you. Orlok takes the way out.
The tower's weather darkens and warms toward Orlok; strangers grow warier and he presses nearer. The Antechamber's dust hangs still — he is almost at the door.

the-tower.content: There is a tower with no door but the one at the bottom, and seven floors between. Men wake at its top with a candle and no memory. The stair goes down. The key to each flight is hidden on the floor it serves. The tower is not a maze; it is a patience.

the-candle.content: The candle is the only clock. It shortens with every act, whether you stand still or run. When it fails, the dark does not hurry. It has been waiting longer than you have.

resources.content: Wax feeds the flame. A match returns a snuffed wick once. Iron keys open iron doors, one floor at a time. Nothing else in the tower is free.

dread.content: The tower keeps a weather. What you do to others changes it: cruelty thickens the dark, mercy thins it. The weather is not a judge; it is a consequence. When it is heavy, the thing at the edge of the light stands nearer.

count-orlok.content: He does not chase. He waits at the edge of the light and lets the light bring you to him. He has no need of haste. He is the creditor; the candle is the debt.

the-survivors.content: Five others are in the tower, each with a candle and a reason. Some will share the light. Some will take it. None of them knows your name until you give it.

warm-and-cold.content: Every kindness spends light now and may return it later. Every cruelty buys light now and spends the one who trusted you. The tower does not care which you choose. It keeps the account.

creatures.content: The creatures are not soldiers. They are taxes. A bat startles the flame; a rat eats the match; a spider keeps what it catches; the pale thing in the dust eats the light and not the flesh. You do not fight them. You decide what to pay.

traps.content: A trap is a door with two prices. One is time; one is a snuffed wick. Read the room before you commit. The safe way is longer, and length is wax.

win-and-loss.content: There are two ways out. The first is your own key and your own light at the bottom door. The second is a door left ajar by someone who reached it first — and a debt the outside will collect. The tower does not care which. It notes which you chose.

sin-pride.content: PRIVATE DESIGN KEY — never state this label or its allegory in prose. Floor 7: a gallery of the same man through the ages; every painted eye follows the flame; the mirror shows the room and not him. Render only the concrete details: the watching portraits, the low candle, the mirror that refuses.

sin-greed.content: PRIVATE DESIGN KEY — never state this label or its allegory in prose. Floor 6: a hoard of strongboxes and coffin earth; a counting woman at a long table; rats richer than the player; a floor of coins that gives way. Render the weight of things, the counting, the appetite that will not spend.

sin-lust.content: PRIVATE DESIGN KEY — never state this label or its allegory in prose. Floor 5: a velvet room, lamplight, a bed of silk and teeth, a woman with an unlit candle, a web that keeps rather than eats. Render the warmth that is not safe, the perfume, the invitation with a price.

sin-envy.content: PRIVATE DESIGN KEY — never state this label or its allegory in prose. Floor 4: glass, specimens, acid, a chalkboard of failed experiments, wolves outside open cages. Render the study of what cannot be possessed, the exact hand, the cold curiosity.

sin-gluttony.content: PRIVATE DESIGN KEY — never state this label or its allegory in prose. Floor 3: a feast gone over, a larder of grey meat, a tallow vat, shades that drain the flame. Render the smell, the plenty that has spoiled, the hunger without a body.

sin-sloth.content: PRIVATE DESIGN KEY — never state this label or its allegory in prose. Floor 2: dust, open coffins, a slow stair, a young man who will not leave, a pale thing that eats the light. Render the kindness of stopping, the weight of the air, the cost of rest.

sin-wrath.content: PRIVATE DESIGN KEY — never state this label or its allegory in prose. Floor 1: scored walls, broken weapons, a locked exit, every creature gathered at the threshold. Render the old violence, the patience at the door, the last muster.

payload.prompt: The candle is already shorter than it was when you woke. What do you do?

choices.label: Search the Spire by candlelight
choices.description: Spend light to find wax or matches before the descent — exploring costs the very thing you're spending to explore.

choices.label: Take the spiralling stair down
choices.description: Trust the descent; the Spire is bare, and every turn here burns wax for nothing.

choices.label: Hold still and watch the thing at the light's edge
choices.description: It has not come closer. Learn how it moves — and whether watching it is worth the wax it costs to stand still.

factions.name: The Survivors
factions.description: Five strangers trapped in Torre Nosferatu, each hunting the exit on their own candle. Not a company — a crowd with the same problem, and not the same answer. They trade, they hoard, they race; warmth and cruelty both count here.
goals: Reach the ground-floor exit before the light runs out
factions.resources: Their own candles, their own wax, and what they can take from one another.

secrets.content: Orlok does not pursue. He cannot cross the light; he holds its edge and collects whoever runs out of it. A snuff without a match is the same door as wax-out.
Ilona was bitten below the third floor. She is his already; what she sells as "the way" is his way. Her candle will never light again.
A survivor who reaches the exit first leaves it ajar only so long as they like you and the tower is calm. Warmth at low Dread holds it longer; a hostile one at high Dread shuts it in your face.

relationships.description: The bite binds her to him. She reads his distance without a candle and cannot flee the dark; what she sells as "knowing the way" is his way, at his price.
Stranger — no prior contact.
Stranger — no prior contact.
Stranger — no prior contact.
Stranger — no prior contact.
Stranger — no prior contact.
The reaper's patient regard. He holds the far rim of your light and waits for it to fail — he does not pursue, he collects.
Opening posture. The innocent sees good in the hoarder and will not stop offering it.
Opening posture. He pities the bitten and keeps trying to light her candle for her.
Opening posture. He distrusts the soft one; softness has cost him before.
Opening posture. He counts her twice and keeps his cache behind him.
Opening posture. Two transactional souls sizing each other up over the same goods.
Opening posture. The archivist marks the bitten as a contradiction she will not write down.
Opening posture. She feels the archivist reading her like a page and turns away.
The rival's regard for the reaper's house — she needs his door and knows it.
The innocent's fear of the thing beyond the light — he does not understand it and will not look.
Opening posture. The archivist has read his ledger and will not say so; he counts her questions as theft.
Opening posture. He will not stand near the unlit candle; he counts her as a debt already spent.
Opening posture. He has counted the dark's arrivals and does not believe in a fair price for them.
Opening posture. The archivist shelters the innocent and has decided he is worth the page it costs.
Opening posture. The archivist keeps her ledger; the broker keeps hers. Neither will show the other the column.
Opening posture. She has read every account of him and trusts none of them.
Opening posture. Two people selling the same dark; each thinks the other is the mark.
Opening posture. He believes her price is a kindness; she lets him.
Member. He keeps his own cache and counts the company as a cost.
Member. She trades with the company and keeps its record.
Member. She walks with them and sells them the distance.
Member. He would not leave them if he could.
Member. She keeps her terms and her own counsel.
Not a member. He is the reason the company exists.

notes.content: At the novel's opening (session zero), the player chooses the protagonist's name — the novel's single interactive door. The name is LOCKED once chosen. It surfaces only where a name can live: the journal header, survivor dialogue, and found documents; narration stays second person ("you"). Until chosen, the entity handles as "You" (character_01). Reconciles the earlier "no name" decision — the name is player-supplied, not absent.

Two layers, disambiguated by name: (1) LORE — the GM-scoped rules-of-the-world entries (the tool's lore field); (2) PAGES — the in-world found fragments the reader encounters (torn pages, inscriptions, scratched warnings), collected and traded. In prose, call the fragments PAGES, never "lore". Canonical-home rule: lore entries carry world-facts; NPC entries carry personality and voice; sync on edit.

Secret reveal triggers (pending; reveal via manage_lore action reveal to the protagonist entity): (1) secret-orlok-collects — revealed on the first sustained near-wax-out or when a found page names the mechanism; (2) secret-ilona-bitten — revealed when Ilona's unlit candle is pressed or she points toward Orlok; (3) secret-borrowed-door — revealed the first time a survivor reaches the exit before you (or a page describes an ajar door). Pages (found fragments) are authored as readable world things in item 8.

Opening beat (Spire): delivers the brief's <30s first success — a Wax Stub within the Spire's first reach; the search choice saves the flame. The figure at the light's edge stays UNNAMED in prose ("something long and thin"); its first naming — by a found page, the tower, or a survivor — is a deliberate later beat. This is the PROLOGUE of the Clinical Witness: concrete, cold, and unhurried.

Guttering-dark grace (the terminal path). On wax-out, or on a snuff with no match in hand, the flame gutters for N turns before Orlok takes you. N is set by Dread, INVERSELY: Dread 0-1 -> 5 turns; 2-3 -> 4; 4-5 -> 3; 6-7 -> 2; 8 -> 1. Low Dread buys a long last chance; high Dread lets him close almost at once. A snuff WITH a match is separate and fully recoverable (re-light, continue) and never enters the grace.

Wax economy. The player starts with The Candle at 30 of 100, and every room transition burns one tick. Seven wax caches restore 10 each, clamped at 100; they lie on the optimal route, so the descent's cost is the walking, not the search. The five survivors carry and burn some of each floor's findable wax — npcs are the main drain — but a survivor's wax is reclaimable: Steal or Bargain while they live, and LOOTABLE from the corpse if they die (to a creature, a trap, or their own wax-out). Matches come in three bundles of two; a bundle adds two, and a relight spends one. WATCH-ITEM: the supply is flat, so later floors are not inherently poorer; the tightening comes from survivors holding more as they accumulate, not a per-floor taper.

Prose pacing follows the R1-R6 design guidance (docs/research/2026-10-11-torre-nosferatu-pursuer-race-research.md): (1) MENACE ARC — Orlok's presence ebbs and flows, nearer as the light fails and receding when the flame is strong; never a constant. (2) FRICTION — each floor is a key -> stair beat; the descent's rhythm is find the key, pay the stair. (3) OBFUSCATED LEAD — never state a rival's exact margin; Nadja is felt "one landing ahead," not measured. (4) RAMPS — a warm alliance (the lantern's wider light) and page-trades that pay off later lift the middle. (5) ANTI-FRUSTRATION — the guttering-dark grace is the last-chance beat, longer at low Dread. (6) POLITICS — survivors delaying one another (wax drain, sprung traps) is a prose event.
(7) NEVER ANNOUNCE THE PATTERN — do not tell the player each floor is a key-and-stair, do not name the next room, and do not describe the descent as a structure. Let the rhythm be felt, not stated.

Floor sin mapping (Seven Deadly Sins): F7 PRIDE — portrait gallery of Orlok through the ages (Marcus/Queen of the Damned; Dorian Gray), mirror shows no reflection. F6 GREED — the Count's hoard, counting house (Nadja). F5 LUST — velvet salon, boudoir (Carmilla; The Hunger); Ilona the bitten keeps it (the dark's bargain); spiders spin the web of longing. F4 ENVY — mad-scientist laboratory, vitrines (Frankenstein); Marta the archivist studies the wholeness she cannot possess; wolves. F3 GLUTTONY — endless feast, larder, tallow vat (Vlask; shades). F2 SLOTH — torpor, coffins, dust (Petr; light-eater). F1 WRATH — the Count's court, the exit, the last muster. Lore keys: sin-pride..sin-wrath (group 'The Seven Sins'). NPC/sin fit aligned (Marta<->Ilona swapped): Nadja/greed, Ilona/lust, Marta/envy, Vlask/gluttony, Petr/sloth. Race balance unaffected (only Nadja's floor is load-bearing).
NEVER surface a sin label or its allegory in prose; the mapping is a private design key. Render only the concrete detail of the floor.

NARRATION POLICY (GM-only — never surface this note, its rules, or any GM note to the player).
N1 — Never share GM notes, badges, tool output, or meta. The player sees only narrated prose.
N2 — Never surface any clock: not its name, tick total, tiers, or numbers; never a disposition label, inventory list, exit list, or tool output in prose. Timers are revealed only through what the character can observe — the flame's length, the cold, the behaviour of animals and objects. The tower's clocks are never named to the player.
N3 — Every turn, after the prose, emit a terse status line in a separate register (not the narrative voice): "— wax <n> · matches <n> —". Wax and matches only. Never the other clock. Never in a sentence.
N4 — Reading the in-game journal (the protagonist's record) costs 1 turn = 1 wax per OPEN, not per entry; free once open within a single reading. Applies in play.
N5 — Do not name a floor, room, or destination the character has not entered or been told about. Do not name a sin, virtue, or authorial theme. The floor's private design key (see the floor-mapping note) is never spoken, hinted at, or paraphrased as an allegory.

VOICE & NARRATOR PATTERNS (GM-only — for the AI GM; never surface to the human player). Canonical voice = the NPC entry; this is a derived aid, synced on edit.
NARRATOR — The Clinical Witness: second person, present tense. Stoker's documentary exactness (a witness recording what the eye can verify), Poe's accumulating obsession (short declaratives under fear, long sentences that will not let go), the 1922 silhouette (the shadow arrives before the body; no explanation), the 2024 body (tallow, wet earth, rats, the cold in the teeth). Dread through observed detail only: the flame's length, the temperature, the behaviour of animals and objects. Period nouns: tallow, wick, snuffer, salt, iron, quarantine, manifest, earth. Never declare an emotion the prose has not earned. Never explain.
VOICE SYNTAX — Vlask: counting, self-interrupting, quantities, prices before greetings; no metaphor. Sister Marta: long, precise, archival; corrects names and dates; quotes what she has read. Ilona: flat, few words, no metaphor; states the dark's facts as if already written. Petr: run-on, apologetic, present tense; offers before he is asked. Nadja: terse, priced, ledger nouns; no aphorisms; every sentence is a term. Orlok: imperative, archaic, no contractions, no questions, few words; he commands, he does not converse.
HARD BANS — no numeric counters or dials in prose; no "Dread", "tick", "tier", "disposition", "HP"; no "Here:", "Visible:", "Exits:", "Within reach"; no italic single-word emphasis for rhythm; no "X does not Y. It Zs." epigrams; no "as if" as the default connective; no naming unvisited floors or rooms; no naming the sin or theme.
PATTERNS — after every turn, a separate status line "— wax N · matches M —"; social actions follow the warm/cold table (Share light, Ally, Bargain, Trade, Steal, Threaten); creatures offer Run (spill wax) or Endure (snuff, needs a match); traps offer Avoid (burn turns/wax) or Spring (snuff, needs a match); Orlok never attacks and speaks only at weather-shifts.

MECHANICAL SCOPE (GM-only) — the tower has NO combat, NO devices, NO vehicles. Creatures are obstacles: the player Runs (spills wax) or Endures (spills wax, snuffs the candle — needs a match) — they are never fought. No initiative, no attack rolls, no hit points, no damage. There are no machines to switch (the candle is a light that burns and can be lit or extinguished) and no vehicles. Verbs in play: go / look / examine, take / drop / inventory, open / close / unlock / lock (doors and the exit), read (pages), light / extinguish (the candle), and the narrative ask / tell / give / show. Do not introduce mechanics the tower lacks.

GRAPH LIMITATIONS (GM-only; updated 2026-11-08). (1) Relationship and location edges now derive in manage_knowledge graph_build; the graph is an INVENTORY plus one-hop edges, not a traversal engine. The five survivors link to The Survivors, and Count Orlok links to it as a rival. (2) Secrets reveal only to ENTITIES (characters); the sole entity is the protagonist ("You"), so revealing a secret would surface it to the human player — therefore all three secrets stay UNREVEALED (known_by empty) by design, to honor the narration policy (N1). (3) The semantic index is bounded to lore / NPC / entity types (24 items); rooms, things, the faction, and countdowns are NOT indexed. (4) graph://novel projections (political/timeline/geography) do not read via the resource surface.

vows.name: Escape Torre Nosferatu
vows.description: Descend the seven floors of Torre Nosferatu, take each floor's key, and reach the ground-floor door — escaping on your own light, not another's wake.

description: Torre Nosferatu — a gothic-horror descent. You wake at the top of a seven-floor tower with one candle and no memory of climbing. Every floor hides a key to the stair down. The wax burns with every step. Five strangers are hunting the same exit, each on their own light. Count Orlok rides the edge of your candle and does not cross it. You name yourself at the opening; the rest you earn on your own light.

seventh floor — spire.name: Seventh Floor — Spire
seventh floor — spire.description: Cold stone, a low ceiling of dark, and walls hung with portraits of the same man. The clothes change; the face does not. Every painted eye is turned toward your candle, and they follow it a beat late, like a room pretending not to watch. The mirror above the sconce gives back the gallery and your face, and the wall behind you — where nothing stands.

seventh floor — wax cache.name: Seventh Floor — Wax Cache
seventh floor — wax cache.description: A gilded niche worked into the wall, its filigree thick with old wax. Someone spent a great deal of light here to be seen doing it. A stub of wax sits in the dust at the bottom.

seventh floor — teaching nest.name: Seventh Floor — Teaching Nest
seventh floor — teaching nest.description: An aviary of empty cages, their gilded doors hanging open. Bats crowd the rafters, thin and restless, their small faces turning toward the flame. None of them scatter. One cage is newer than the rest; its bars are clean.

seventh floor — grand stair.name: Seventh Floor — Grand Stair
seventh floor — grand stair.description: A marble descent, every step polished, every wall angled to flatter a single figure walking down. The stair is cold underfoot. At its head, an iron door.

seventh floor — connector 1.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 1
seventh floor — connector 1.description: A narrow passage, the walls canted a few degrees off true. The candle reaches the first sconce and no further. Something has scratched the plaster at shoulder height, over and over.

seventh floor — connector 2.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 2
seventh floor — connector 2.description: A dead end. Dust has settled in a long drift against the wall, and a cold draught moves through it from somewhere that has no opening. The air smells of stone and old rain.

seventh floor — connector 3.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 3
seventh floor — connector 3.description: The corridor turns back on itself. You pass four sconces, then a fifth you would swear you have passed already. The flame leans as you walk, as if the air is following you.

seventh floor — connector 4.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 4
seventh floor — connector 4.description: A landing. A black ring is scorched into the boards, wax run and set and never scraped away. Someone's light ended here, and no one came back for the candle.

seventh floor — connector 5.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 5
seventh floor — connector 5.description: A cramped turn where the stone sweats. The ceiling is close enough to touch. Your flame hisses faintly and throws its light short; the walls drink it.

seventh floor — connector 6.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 6
seventh floor — connector 6.description: An alcove lined with empty iron sconces, every wick burned to a black stub. The metal is cold. It smells of soot and old iron, and nothing else.

seventh floor — connector 7.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 7
seventh floor — connector 7.description: A window-slit, its glass gone to teeth. Beyond it there is no sky and no ground — only a flat black that your breath does not fog. The draught comes off it steadily, inward.

seventh floor — connector 8.name: Seventh Floor — Connector 8
seventh floor — connector 8.description: A short stone bridge over a shaft. The candlelight goes down a few feet and stops. There is no rail. The air rising from below is cold and slow.

sixth floor — entry landing.name: Sixth Floor — Entry Landing
sixth floor — entry landing.description: The stair arrives among strongboxes stacked to the ceiling, and coffins packed with dark earth. A hinge somewhere in the stacks eases open a finger's width, then holds. The candle does not reach the top of the room.

sixth floor — grand stair.name: Sixth Floor — Grand Stair
sixth floor — grand stair.description: A stair of dark wood, each tread inlaid with a coin that rings faintly underfoot. At the head, an iron door. The coins go quiet at the threshold, as if listening.

sixth floor — key room.name: Sixth Floor — Key Room
sixth floor — key room.description: A vault. Gold lies heaped in a shallow nest at the centre — coins, plate, a child's cup, rings like gravel. The key rests on top, plain iron. The heap shifts a finger's width when the air moves.

sixth floor — wax refill.name: Sixth Floor — Wax Refill
sixth floor — wax refill.description: A shrine-table crowded with votive cups, each pooled with wax gone dark and old. Some of it is still soft. The room smells of cold incense and tallow.

sixth floor — social hall.name: Sixth Floor — Social Hall
sixth floor — social hall.description: A long table under a dead chandelier, ledgers stacked like masonry. A woman sits at the near end with her own candle, working a column. She does not look up until she has finished it.

sixth floor — trap hall.name: Sixth Floor — Trap Hall
sixth floor — trap hall.description: The floor is not a floor. Coins and plate are heaped over a sag in the boards, and where the heap meets the wall a hairline crack runs joint to joint. Dust sifts through it in a thin, steady trickle.

sixth floor — beast warren.name: Sixth Floor — Beast Warren
sixth floor — beast warren.description: Rats move in a brown tide, each dragging something bright — a coin, a ring, a candle stub carried like a trophy. They gnaw through coin and match alike. They are not afraid of the light.

sixth floor — connector 1.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 1
sixth floor — connector 1.description: A passage whose walls lean toward each other. The dark between the sconces is complete. Somewhere ahead, something drags and stops, as if it heard you stop too.

sixth floor — connector 2.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 2
sixth floor — connector 2.description: A landing with a dead lantern on a hook, its wick cold and black. The glass is smoked. A bundle of matches lies half under its base.

sixth floor — connector 3.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 3
sixth floor — connector 3.description: A corridor that doubles back. No sconce is lit. Two candles would make two circles here; one makes a single small room that moves with you.

sixth floor — connector 4.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 4
sixth floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn. Low on the stone, at knee height, someone has scratched a warning with a nail: WE WENT ROUND. IT STILL TOOK HER. Beneath it, a row of small tally marks.

sixth floor — connector 5.name: Sixth Floor — Connector 5
sixth floor — connector 5.description: An alcove. A torn page lies flat on the stone where someone dropped it and did not come back for it. The dust around it is disturbed in one direction only — toward the page.

fifth floor — entry landing.name: Fifth Floor — Entry Landing
fifth floor — entry landing.description: The stair arrives behind a heavy velvet curtain. Beyond it: mirrors angled wrong, and a low red glow that is not your candle. The air is thick with perfume and old smoke.

fifth floor — grand stair.name: Fifth Floor — Grand Stair
fifth floor — grand stair.description: A stair hung with velvet. The cloth eats the sound of your steps so completely that you keep checking your feet are moving. At the head, an iron door.

fifth floor — key room.name: Fifth Floor — Key Room
fifth floor — key room.description: A low room of silk the colour of a bruise. A bed, a vanity, two cups of wine — one full, one already poured. The key lies on a silk pillow between them.

fifth floor — wax refill.name: Fifth Floor — Wax Refill
fifth floor — wax refill.description: A marble basin brimming with warm wax. A skin has begun to set on the surface, as though someone stepped out a moment ago. The surface still trembles.

fifth floor — social hall.name: Fifth Floor — Social Hall
fifth floor — social hall.description: Leather chairs, lamplight, a gramophone turning out a thin waltz with no one winding it. A woman rises from a chair as if she had been waiting exactly this long. Her candle is unlit.

fifth floor — trap hall.name: Fifth Floor — Trap Hall
fifth floor — trap hall.description: A bed the size of a small room, hung in silk. The sheets are knotted into a pattern no body makes in sleep. The silk is dark in places that are not shadows, and it moves very slightly, as if breathing.

fifth floor — beast warren.name: Fifth Floor — Beast Warren
fifth floor — beast warren.description: Doorways laced floor to lintel with webbing. The webbing is soft, not dusty; it flexes when the light touches it, and closes again where it is torn. Spiders hang in the strands like dark fruit.

fifth floor — connector 1.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 1
fifth floor — connector 1.description: A passage whose walls are faintly warm to the touch. The perfume follows you in. The dark between the sconces is not quite empty; something in it keeps the same pace you do.

fifth floor — connector 2.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 2
fifth floor — connector 2.description: A landing of cold iron sconces and dust. The dust is undisturbed except for one line of footprints that stop in the middle of the floor and do not go on.

fifth floor — connector 3.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 3
fifth floor — connector 3.description: A corridor that doubles back. There is no sconce lit anywhere in it. The walls are closer than they were, or you are more tired than you thought.

fifth floor — connector 4.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 4
fifth floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn with a shelf of paper gone soft with rot — ledgers, letters, a few loose pages. One has slid clear of the rest.

fifth floor — connector 5.name: Fifth Floor — Connector 5
fifth floor — connector 5.description: A short bridge over a shaft. The candlelight reaches a few feet down and stops. The draught rising out of the dark carries the perfume up with it.

fourth floor — entry landing.name: Fourth Floor — Entry Landing
fourth floor — entry landing.description: The stair arrives among glass, cold metal, and the smell of formaldehyde. Vitrines line the landing, each holding something preserved: a hand, a bird with too many eyes, a face that is almost yours. Every case is labelled in a small, exact hand.

fourth floor — grand stair.name: Fourth Floor — Grand Stair
fourth floor — grand stair.description: A stair of glass treads, each reflecting a room you have not reached — a hall of candles, a door of teeth, a face at a window. The reflections do not move when you do.

fourth floor — key room.name: Fourth Floor — Key Room
fourth floor — key room.description: A cabinet of jars, shelf after shelf, each holding a shape in cloudy fluid and a label in the same exact hand. The key sits in one jar among them, its iron gone soft and grey through the glass.

fourth floor — wax refill.name: Fourth Floor — Wax Refill
fourth floor — wax refill.description: Copper stills, cold now, and wax rendered drip by drip into a trough. The room smells of fat and hot metal. The wax in the trough has set unevenly, like something cooled while moving.

fourth floor — social hall.name: Fourth Floor — Social Hall
fourth floor — social hall.description: A laboratory. Vitrines of specimens, a chalkboard dense with failed experiments, each row crossed out and dated. A woman stands at the board with chalk in hand and finishes the line before she turns.

fourth floor — trap hall.name: Fourth Floor — Trap Hall
fourth floor — trap hall.description: A case of glass and acid, its seams weeping a thin line that hisses where it touches the floor. The cracks in the glass run in one direction. Where they stop, the acid has spent itself.

fourth floor — beast warren.name: Fourth Floor — Beast Warren
fourth floor — beast warren.description: Cages stand open, and the wolves stand outside them — thin, grey, pacing the bars they no longer need. They do not look at you. They look at each other, and at the empty cages.

fourth floor — connector 1.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 1
fourth floor — connector 1.description: A passage under a smell of dust and old paper. The sconces are cold. Something has been dragged along one wall, leaving a clean stripe in the grime.

fourth floor — connector 2.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 2
fourth floor — connector 2.description: A landing with a scorched mark where a candle died. The mark is old, but the wax around it is fresh, as if someone set a new candle in the same place and thought better of it.

fourth floor — connector 3.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 3
fourth floor — connector 3.description: A corridor that doubles back. No sconce is lit. The air is dry and still, and your flame stands straight up, as if it is being watched.

fourth floor — connector 4.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 4
fourth floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn, the ceiling too near. The stone is cold. A row of small marks is scratched at eye height, too regular to be damage.

fourth floor — connector 5.name: Fourth Floor — Connector 5
fourth floor — connector 5.description: An alcove with a scratched warning low on the stone. The letters are worn; only the shape of them remains, and the shape is a hand pressed flat.

third floor — entry landing.name: Third Floor — Entry Landing
third floor — entry landing.description: The stair arrives into the smell of a feast gone over — meat sweetening, wine souring, candles burned down into the bones of themselves. Long tables recede into the dark, every plate heaped, every chair pushed back.

third floor — grand stair.name: Third Floor — Grand Stair
third floor — grand stair.description: A stair so wide it could seat a banquet along it. The faint marks on the steps suggest it once did. At the head, an iron door.

third floor — key room.name: Third Floor — Key Room
third floor — key room.description: Hooks line the ceiling, and from them hang cuts of meat gone grey and dry. They do not smell like meat. The key hangs from a hook between them, iron and plain.

third floor — wax refill.name: Third Floor — Wax Refill
third floor — wax refill.description: A great copper vat, brimming with wax still warm. A scum of something darker floats on the top. The whole room smells of rendered fat and old feast.

third floor — social hall.name: Third Floor — Social Hall
third floor — social hall.description: Long tables laid for a dinner that has lasted centuries — trenchers of dust, cups of something that used to be wine. At the far end, a small, careful man works the underside of a table with both hands.

third floor — trap hall.name: Third Floor — Trap Hall
third floor — trap hall.description: A long table stripped to bone-white wood. Beneath it the floor is a puzzle of boards that no longer lie flat. The centre boards gape, and something under them shifts when the air moves.

third floor — beast warren.name: Third Floor — Beast Warren
third floor — beast warren.description: Old straw, old troughs, and shades moving through the walls like smoke through a grate — thin, hungry, not quite shaped. They gather toward the light, and where they press close the flame leans and thins.

third floor — connector 1.name: Third Floor — Connector 1
third floor — connector 1.description: A passage that smells of cold grease. A plate has been left on the floor against the wall, and the dust on it is undisturbed. The sconces are empty.

third floor — connector 2.name: Third Floor — Connector 2
third floor — connector 2.description: A landing of empty iron sconces, all cold. The floor is sticky in one place, as if something was spilled and never wiped.

third floor — connector 3.name: Third Floor — Connector 3
third floor — connector 3.description: A corridor that doubles back. There is no sconce lit. The air is warmer here than it should be, and it carries a smell of tallow.

third floor — connector 4.name: Third Floor — Connector 4
third floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn, the stone slick with damp. The water catches the candlelight and gives it back doubled, so the corridor looks wider than it is.

third floor — connector 5.name: Third Floor — Connector 5
third floor — connector 5.description: A short bridge over a shaft. The candlelight goes down a few feet and stops. The air rising from below is warm, and it smells of the feast.

second floor — entry landing.name: Second Floor — Entry Landing
second floor — entry landing.description: The stair arrives into dust deep enough to hush it. The dust lies in soft, undisturbed dunes. The silence is so complete that your own breathing sounds like an interruption.

second floor — grand stair.name: Second Floor — Grand Stair
second floor — grand stair.description: A slow stair, each step deeper in dust than the last, as if it is falling asleep going down. At the head, an iron door.

second floor — key room.name: Second Floor — Key Room
second floor — key room.description: A single coffin stands open on a stone bier, its lid leaned against the wall. The key lies in the dust inside it — shallow enough to see, deep enough that you would have to put your hand in.

second floor — wax refill.name: Second Floor — Wax Refill
second floor — wax refill.description: Wax has pooled in the low places and set under years of settled dust — a grey, soft landscape of it. It is the first thing here that looks peaceful and means it.

second floor — social hall.name: Second Floor — Social Hall
second floor — social hall.description: Coffins stand open along the walls, cobwebbed and empty. The air is thick enough to lean on. A young man sits on the edge of one with a candle stub in both hands, and he stands when he sees you.

second floor — trap hall.name: Second Floor — Trap Hall
second floor — trap hall.description: The floor is covered in dust, and the dust lies in a soft blanket — except where it dips, in a wide oval at the centre, too smooth to be natural. The edge stands in little ridges.

second floor — beast warren.name: Second Floor — Beast Warren
second floor — beast warren.description: It lies against the far wall in the dark, half-asleep: a soft pale mass the size of a cart, with a mouth that opens and closes like slow breathing. It has no eyes. It turns toward heat, and toward light.

second floor — connector 1.name: Second Floor — Connector 1
second floor — connector 1.description: A passage where the dust is thinner. The sconces are cold. Small bare footprints cross the floor in slow circles and never leave the corridor.

second floor — connector 2.name: Second Floor — Connector 2
second floor — connector 2.description: A landing with a dead lantern someone left behind. Beside it, half under the base, a small bundle of matches, dry and still usable.

second floor — connector 3.name: Second Floor — Connector 3
second floor — connector 3.description: A corridor that doubles back. No sconce is lit. The dust lies in a soft even blanket, just beginning to be disturbed by your feet.

second floor — connector 4.name: Second Floor — Connector 4
second floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn with a shelf of paper gone to mush. Whatever was written there is not readable now. One scrap has stayed dry near the back.

second floor — connector 5.name: Second Floor — Connector 5
second floor — connector 5.description: An alcove where a torn page lies where someone dropped it. The dust has gathered only at its edges, as if the page had been set down carefully.

first floor — entry landing.name: First Floor — Entry Landing
first floor — entry landing.description: The stair arrives at the bottom of the tower, into cold air and old violence. The walls are scored and gouged. The air tastes of iron.

first floor — antechamber.name: First Floor — Antechamber
first floor — antechamber.description: Dust, a dead lantern, and an ancestral portrait whose painted eyes track the flame. On the far wall, the exit: heavy, iron-bound, locked. Cold air seeps around it. Beyond it is outside.

first floor — key room.name: First Floor — Key Room
first floor — key room.description: Broken weapons lie everywhere — spears snapped at the haft, swords bent, shields staved in. Every point and edge is turned toward the door you came through. The key rests on the flat of a shattered blade at the centre.

first floor — wax refill.name: First Floor — Wax Refill
first floor — wax refill.description: Wax pooled and hardened over old burns. The burns are shaped like hands. The room is cold, and the wax is cold, and it does not soften under your fingers.

first floor — trap hall.name: First Floor — Trap Hall
first floor — trap hall.description: The floor is a cracked ruin of flagstones, the cracks running in long faults from wall to wall. The faults are widest at the centre and narrow toward the east wall, where the stones still key into their neighbours.

first floor — beast warren.name: First Floor — Beast Warren
first floor — beast warren.description: Every creature the tower holds is gathered here, thickest near the exit — a pale bulk, wolves, rats, spiders hanging in ropes, shapes without names. They do not attack. They stand in the way and watch the candles.

first floor — connector 1.name: First Floor — Connector 1
first floor — connector 1.description: A passage whose walls are gouged deeper than the others. Some of the gouges are old; some are not. The sconces are cold.

first floor — connector 2.name: First Floor — Connector 2
first floor — connector 2.description: A landing of cold iron sconces and settled dust. A bundle of matches lies within reach, wrapped in waxed thread.

first floor — connector 3.name: First Floor — Connector 3
first floor — connector 3.description: A corridor that doubles back. No sconce is lit. The gouges here are in sets of five, as if something counted its way along the wall.

first floor — connector 4.name: First Floor — Connector 4
first floor — connector 4.description: A cramped turn, the ceiling too near. The stone is scored in long parallel lines. The air smells of rust and old smoke.

first floor — connector 5.name: First Floor — Connector 5
first floor — connector 5.description: An alcove with a scratched warning low on the stone — the same hand as the tally marks above. Beside it lies a torn page, still readable.

first floor — connector 6.name: First Floor — Connector 6
first floor — connector 6.description: A short bridge of stone over a shaft that drops into the dark below. The draught from the shaft is cold and clean — the first clean air since the top of the tower.

beyond the threshold.name: Beyond the Threshold
beyond the threshold.description: Outside. Cold air, the tower wall at your back, and a dark that belongs to the world — not to him. The candle flame stands straight up now, no longer leaning, no longer watched.

sixth floor — dust passage.name: Sixth Floor — Dust Passage
sixth floor — dust passage.description: A service passage behind the trap hall, narrow and furred with dust. The walls are scratched at shoulder height, as if something counted its way along them.

sixth floor — narrow turn.name: Sixth Floor — Narrow Turn
sixth floor — narrow turn.description: The passage pinches to a shoulder's width and turns. A cold draft comes from the far side, carrying the smell of old stone and dry paper.

sixth floor — collapsed landing.name: Sixth Floor — Collapsed Landing
sixth floor — collapsed landing.description: A landing half fallen in, its stones stepped down like a broken stair. The way east is clear if you watch your feet.

fourth floor — bone passage.name: Fourth Floor — Bone Passage
fourth floor — bone passage.description: A servants' passage behind the laboratory wall, its floor gritty with chalk and splintered glass. A row of specimen labels has been pasted over the plaster.

fourth floor — cold turn.name: Fourth Floor — Cold Turn
fourth floor — cold turn.description: The passage narrows and turns beside a cold flue. Something has been scrubbed from the wall, but the scrubbing left a shape.

fourth floor — fallen landing.name: Fourth Floor — Fallen Landing
fourth floor — fallen landing.description: A landing under a fallen beam, the way ahead low and awkward. The beam is chalked with a date that has been crossed out twice.

second floor — dust passage.name: Second Floor — Dust Passage
second floor — dust passage.description: A service passage behind the sleeping hall, its air thick and warm. Dust lies in the seams of the boards, undisturbed except for one long track.

second floor — quiet turn.name: Second Floor — Quiet Turn
second floor — quiet turn.description: The passage turns beside a sealed door. No sound comes through it, not even the tower's breathing.

second floor — sunken landing.name: Second Floor — Sunken Landing
second floor — sunken landing.description: A landing sunk a hand's depth into the floor, its stones soft with damp. The way east is clear if you step where the dust has already been broken.

your candle.name: Your Candle
your candle.description: A candle in a brass dish. Its flame reaches a few feet and no further. The wax is already lower than it was when you woke.

seventh floor key.name: Seventh Floor Key
seventh floor key.description: A heavy iron key with a bow cast as a closed eye. It is cold to the touch, and it opens the stair down from the Spire.

seventh floor stair door.name: Seventh Floor Stair Door
seventh floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the caged stair down. Locked; the seventh floor's key opens it.
seventh floor stair door.noise: A low groan of old hinges.

wax stub.name: Wax Stub
wax stub.description: A stub of candle-wax pressed into the stone beneath a portrait. It will buy back a little light.

sixth floor key.name: Sixth Floor Key
sixth floor key.description: A heavy iron key, its bow stamped with a coin worn nearly smooth. It opens the stair down from the sixth floor.

sixth floor stair door.name: Sixth Floor Stair Door
sixth floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the coin-inlaid stair down to the fifth floor. Locked; the sixth floor's key opens it.

sixth floor wax.name: Sixth Floor Wax
sixth floor wax.description: A votive cup of wax, dark at the rim and still soft beneath. It will buy back a little light.

matches (sixth).name: Matches (Sixth)
matches (sixth).description: Two matches bound with waxed thread. A snuff is survivable only while one of these remains.

page — the count waits.name: Page — The Count Waits
page — the count waits.description: A torn page, dropped where someone stopped to read it.
page — the count waits.read_text: "...he does not follow. I have run from him for six days and he has not followed once. He is always at the edge of the lamp when I stop. It is the stopping he waits for."

fifth floor key.name: Fifth Floor Key
fifth floor key.description: A slim iron key on a length of velvet cord, warm from a hand that is no longer here. It opens the stair down from the fifth floor.

fifth floor stair door.name: Fifth Floor Stair Door
fifth floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the velvet-hung stair down to the fourth floor. Locked; the fifth floor's key opens it.

fifth floor wax.name: Fifth Floor Wax
fifth floor wax.description: Pooled wax under a sconce — the fifth floor's guaranteed refill.

page — the bitten.name: Page — The Bitten
page — the bitten.description: A torn page in an archivist's hand.
page — the bitten.read_text: "...she will not light her candle. Do not ask her to. She has already paid for the dark and does not wish to be reminded of the price."

fourth floor key.name: Fourth Floor Key
fourth floor key.description: A glass-headed key, its iron teeth clouded with old fluid. It opens the stair down from the fourth floor.

fourth floor stair door.name: Fourth Floor Stair Door
fourth floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the glass stair down to the third floor. Locked; the fourth floor's key opens it.

fourth floor wax.name: Fourth Floor Wax
fourth floor wax.description: Pooled, re-hardened wax — the fourth floor's guaranteed refill.

page — the borrowed door.name: Page — The Borrowed Door
page — the borrowed door.description: A torn page, scratched over with a warning.
page — the borrowed door.read_text: "...if another reaches the door first, it may stand open a while. I do not know how long. I know that the one who slips out behind another does not sleep well after."

third floor key.name: Third Floor Key
third floor key.description: A greasy iron key, its bow hooked like a butcher's ring. It opens the stair down from the third floor.

third floor stair door.name: Third Floor Stair Door
third floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the wide banquet stair down to the second floor. Locked; the third floor's key opens it.

third floor wax.name: Third Floor Wax
third floor wax.description: Pooled wax — the third floor's guaranteed refill.

second floor key.name: Second Floor Key
second floor key.description: A tarnished iron key, furred with dust. It opens the stair down from the second floor.

second floor stair door.name: Second Floor Stair Door
second floor stair door.description: The iron door at the head of the dust-choked stair down to the first floor. Locked; the second floor's key opens it.

second floor wax.name: Second Floor Wax
second floor wax.description: Pooled wax — the second floor's guaranteed refill.

first floor key.name: First Floor Key
first floor key.description: The ground-floor iron key — the bow that opens the exit. The reliable way out, and the only one that is fully your own.

the exit door.name: The Exit Door
the exit door.description: Heavy, iron-bound, and locked. The only way out. It does not open to the dark, and it does not open to another's passing — only to the key, and to your own light.

first floor wax.name: First Floor Wax
first floor wax.description: Pooled wax — the first floor's guaranteed refill.

matches (fourth).name: Matches (Fourth)
matches (fourth).description: Two matches bound with waxed thread. A snuff is survivable only while one of these remains.

matches (second).name: Matches (Second)
matches (second).description: Two matches bound with waxed thread. A snuff is survivable only while one of these remains.

page — the weather.name: Page — The Weather
page — the weather.description: A torn page pinned behind a portrait whose eyes no longer follow it.
page — the weather.read_text: "...the sky is not the sky here. It answers the hand. I have seen it darken when I was cruel, and clear when I was kind, and I do not know which of us it was watching."

page — the key.name: Page — The Key
page — the key.description: A torn page on a feasting table, under a plate no one has lifted in years.
page — the key.read_text: "...the key is always in the room that feels safest. That is the cruelty of it. The danger is the walking between."

page — the torpor.name: Page — The Torpor
page — the torpor.description: A torn page in the dust of a coffin room.
page — the torpor.read_text: "...the dust here is kind. That is the danger. It asks nothing of you but that you stop."

page — the last muster.name: Page — The Last Muster
page — the last muster.description: A torn page near the exit, held down by an old weapon.
page — the last muster.read_text: "...they do not guard the door. They only wait to see whether the light or the fear gives out first."

subjective_memory.gist: I woke on cold stone with one candle and no memory of climbing.
The candle was already shorter than it should have been.
Something long and thin stood at the edge of the light and did not come closer.
The new one woke on the top floor tonight with one candle. Easy to outlast.
I spent a match to keep my own stub alive rather than share it. It was the correct trade.
The new arrival reads like a solicitor. Wants information before light. I have the former to spare.
The tower's regions contradict each other. I collect the disagreement; it is the only map that holds.
He is nearer tonight than the candle says. I could tell them how near. That is worth a match or two.
I have not lit the candle since the bite. I carry it only so they think I am like them.
I gave half my wax to a stranger on the fifth landing. They did not thank me. It was still right.

claim.subject: giving light
claim.object: right even when it is not returned

subjective_memory.gist: If I die down here, I hope it is while someone else's candle is lit.
One landing ahead, as always. Let them follow my crumbs. It costs nothing and keeps them slow.
If I reach the door first, I will leave it ajar. For a price, of course.
It has brought a solicitor. They always bring paper and purpose into my dark. Let it descend.
It saved the match. Good. The longer the flame, the longer the walk to me.

facets.value: A solicitor who came to Torre Nosferatu on a client's business.
Keep the record exact, whatever the dark does.
Find a way out of the tower.
Admit that the record cannot save you.
Being forgotten in the dark, with no one left to read the record.
The doors were locked behind you, and no one came when you called.
You were sent to be a witness, not to return.
The tower is a thing to be survived, not understood.
The record is the only thing keeping the fear in order.
Never spend the last match to light a page.
Write everything down, even when the hand shakes.
The hoarder of the third floor.
A fair count is the only kindness he trusts.
Being left with nothing to count.
